transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
Ever since they cut my hours and dumped all this paperwork on me, I just haven’t been handling it well. I feel like I’m reacting all wrong to everything at work.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or do you find it hard to feel pleasure in daily activities?

Yeah, I've definitely stopped doing things I usually love. I've been skipping my rec league games and turning down side jobs with my buddies because I'm just too wound up and embarrassed about how I'm handling everything. I feel like I can't keep up with anything right now.
Are you feeling more worried or on edge most of the time, or is your main struggle feeling down, hopeless, or worthless?

I’m definitely more on edge and worried most of the time, rather than feeling hopeless or worthless. I just feel constantly wound up and tense, always stressed that I'm going to snap or mess up on this paperwork. It's really embarrassing because I feel like I just can't keep up with any of it.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F32", "F41.1"], but based on this conversation, F32 (depressive episode) seems less likely because the patient explicitly states that their main struggle is not feeling hopeless or worthless, but rather being on edge, worried, and tense. They report loss of interest in activities, which could support depression, but the predominant mood is anxiety and stress related to work performance and fear of failure, aligning more closely with generalized anxiety disorder (F41.1). Therefore, F32 is dropped from the list and F41.1 remains as the most consistent diagnosis.
